usage.selection_rule: Use 5-10 questions per session. Stop when answers stop producing concrete evidence.
usage.follow_up_rule: Ask for recent examples, contrasts, choices not taken, and disconfirming evidence before interpreting.
usage.output_rule: Record evidence before interpretation and mark confidence for every synthesis.

questions.prompt: Walk through the five decisions or events that most changed the direction of your life, in chronological order.
questions.follow_up: What changed immediately afterward in your behavior, relationships, or resources?

questions.prompt: Which environments have made you feel unusually capable, and which have made you feel unusually limited?
questions.follow_up: What was present or absent in each environment?

questions.prompt: What recurring responsibilities or constraints shaped your early habits?
questions.follow_up: Which habits from that period still show up now?

questions.prompt: Which transition was harder than you expected, and what did you actually do when the difficulty appeared?
questions.follow_up: What would you do differently with the same constraints?

questions.prompt: What part of your history do you tend to omit when presenting yourself to others?
questions.follow_up: Why does that omission feel necessary, and what would change if it were included?

questions.prompt: What do people reliably ask you to help with, and what do you actually deliver?
questions.follow_up: Give one recent example and one example where the pattern did not hold.

questions.prompt: Give three examples where your contribution produced a visible result. What exactly did you do?
questions.follow_up: Which part was unique to you, and which part was shared?

questions.prompt: How do you learn a new method? Recall a recent example from beginning to usable skill.
questions.follow_up: What slowed you down, and what made the method finally click?

questions.prompt: Where do you produce results disproportionate to effort, and where does effort fail to produce results?
questions.follow_up: What differs between those two situations?

questions.prompt: Which artifact best represents how you work, and why did you choose it?
questions.follow_up: What does it reveal that a verbal description would miss?

questions.prompt: Describe a consequential decision in detail. What did you notice, ignore, consider, and choose?
questions.follow_up: What did you know only after the decision?

questions.prompt: When evidence conflicts with intuition, what do you do? Give a specific example.
questions.follow_up: When has either side been wrong?

questions.prompt: How do you decide that a problem is worth working on?
questions.follow_up: What kinds of problems do you reject even when they are prestigious or well paid?

questions.prompt: Recall a time you changed your mind. What evidence or experience caused the change?
questions.follow_up: What made the old belief attractive in the first place?

questions.prompt: What kind of uncertainty is most difficult for you to tolerate, and how do you respond to it?
questions.follow_up: Describe a time you acted before you felt certain.

questions.prompt: What do you repeatedly spend time, attention, or money on even without external reward?
questions.follow_up: What need or value does that activity serve?

questions.prompt: What have you sacrificed for a principle, and what would you refuse to sacrifice?
questions.follow_up: How has that boundary changed over time?

questions.prompt: When do you feel most engaged, and when do you become drained or detached?
questions.follow_up: What is the observable behavior at each extreme?

questions.prompt: Which praise or criticism stays with you, and why does it land so strongly?
questions.follow_up: Does the reaction reveal a standard, fear, or aspiration?

questions.prompt: What future outcome would still feel meaningful if nobody recognized you for it?
questions.follow_up: What current choice is aligned or misaligned with that outcome?

questions.prompt: How does your behavior change with peers, authorities, clients, or people you lead?
questions.follow_up: What stays consistent across all of them?

questions.prompt: Describe a conflict where you were partly wrong. What did you do afterward?
questions.follow_up: What repair strategy worked or failed?

questions.prompt: What feedback do others give you repeatedly, and which parts do you accept or reject?
questions.follow_up: What evidence supports each response?

questions.prompt: In a team, what role do you naturally take before anyone assigns one?
questions.follow_up: When has that role helped, and when has it become a limitation?

questions.prompt: What environmental conditions reliably help you think, produce, and recover?
questions.follow_up: What conditions do you keep tolerating even though they do not work?

questions.prompt: Choose a repeated pattern. What are two competing explanations for it?
questions.follow_up: What evidence would distinguish them?

questions.prompt: Where does your self-description differ from what your behavior or others suggest?
questions.follow_up: Which account has stronger evidence, and in what context?

questions.prompt: What would a thoughtful critic say is your most important blind spot?
questions.follow_up: How would you test whether the criticism is accurate?

questions.prompt: Describe three plausible futures: one likely, one desired, and one feared. What choices lead toward each?
questions.follow_up: Which choice is reversible, and which is costly to reverse?

questions.prompt: What small experiment in the next 30 days would test an important uncertainty in this profile?
questions.follow_up: What observable result would confirm, weaken, or complicate the current interpretation?
